Lamarck was quite similar to Darwin, but held beliefs that were essentially debunked. Lamarck held that you could change your traits throughout your lifetime, and that these traits could be passed on to your young. The effects of Darwinian evolution are likely much stronger than the effects of Lamarckian evolution, but modern day "epigenetics" goes to show that Lamarck was not all wrong. Epigenetics shows us that genes can be expressed at different strengths, by the amount of proteins they create. If a certain trait is exercised enough, you can increase the strength at which this gene is expressed, and this "imprint" onto your genetic code can be passed on to your descendants.
